extracted.intended_audience: debt collectors, compliance officers at debt collection agencies, creditors who collect debts, and their legal counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluate or implement compliance with 12 CFR Part 1006 (Regulation F) — the CFPB rules implementing the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act — covering permissible communications, prohibited practices, disclosure and validation notice requirements, recordkeeping, and related procedures for debt collectors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority, purpose, and coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: This part (Regulation F) implements the FDCPA and related statutes to eliminate abusive debt collection practices, protect consumers, promote consistent State action, prescribe disclosure requirements, and impose record retention to enable Bureau supervision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains statutory authorities (15 U.S.C. and 12 U.S.C.), scope applying to debt collectors as defined in §1006.2(i), and notes exceptions (see §1006.108 and appendix A for State exemptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions (key terms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions of terms used throughout the part, including 'attempt to communicate', 'communicate', 'consumer', 'consumer financial product or service', 'creditor', 'debt', 'debt collector', 'limited-content message', 'person', and 'State'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many compliance obligations turn on these definitions; for example, the detailed definition of 'debt collector' (including when creditors using another name are collectors) and the required/optional content of a 'limited-content message' are substantive regulatory requirements (see §1006.2(i) and (j)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibitions regarding communications at unusual or inconvenient times or places (§1006.6(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Debt collectors must not communicate or attempt to communicate with a consumer at any unusual time or a time the debt collector knows or should know is inconvenient; absent contrary knowledge, before 8:00 a.m. or after 9:00 p.m. local time is inconvenient. Also prohibits communications at unusual or inconvenient places.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions only as provided in §1006.6(b)(4) (prior consent or court permission). This is an express per-communication prohibition (applies to calls, texts, emails, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on communicating with consumers represented by an attorney (§1006.6(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Debt collectors must not communicate with a consumer if they know the consumer is represented by an attorney regarding the debt and know or can readily ascertain the attorney's name and address, unless the attorney fails to respond in a reasonable time or consents to direct communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies except where paragraph (b)(4) exceptions apply (prior consent/court permission).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on communicating at consumer's place of employment (§1006.6(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Debt collectors must not communicate with a consumer at the consumer's place of employment if they know or have reason to know the employer prohibits such communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subject to the exceptions in §1006.6(b)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to timing/place/representation prohibitions (§1006.6(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: The prohibitions on unusual times/places, attorney-represented consumers, and communications at work do not apply if the consumer gave prior consent directly to the debt collector during a lawful communication, or if a court of competent jurisdiction expressly permits the communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior consent must be given directly and during a communication that itself does not violate prohibitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cease communication after refusal to pay or notice to cease (§1006.6(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a consumer notifies a debt collector in writing that they refuse to pay or want the collector to cease communications, the collector must not communicate further with respect to that debt, except to (i) advise termination of efforts, (ii) notify of possible/ordinary remedies, or (iii) notify intent to invoke a specified remedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to written notices; exceptions are narrow and limited to specified informational communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on communication with third parties (§1006.6(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Debt collectors must not communicate, in connection with the collection of any debt, with any person other than: the consumer, the consumer's attorney, a consumer reporting agency (if permitted), the creditor, the creditor's attorney, or the debt collector's attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions in §1006.6(d)(2) include communications to acquire location information, prior consumer consent, court permission, or as reasonably necessary to effectuate a postjudgment remedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable procedures to avoid third-party disclosure errors for email/text (§1006.6(d)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Debt collectors must maintain procedures reasonably adapted to avoid bona fide errors that would result in sending email/text communications to third parties in violation of the third-party communication prohibition; procedures must reasonably confirm/document that the collector communicated to the consumer's authorized address/number and did not use an address/number known to have resulted in prohibited disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes the need to confirm address/number provenance before use and documentation steps. This is an FDCPA section 813(c) bona fide error protection measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for using email addresses (§1006.6(d)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: A debt collector may send email to an address only if (i) consumer used that email to communicate and hasn't opted out or gave prior consent, (ii) creditor obtained and used the email and provided written/electronic notice to the consumer (with specific disclosures and opt-out mechanism with at least 35 days), or (iii) prior debt collector obtained and used the email in accordance with these procedures and consumer didn't opt out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If relying on creditor-based procedures the creditor must have provided clear notice that the debt will be transferred, that the collector may use the email, opt-out instructions, and specified timing; domain must be public unless provided by employer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for using telephone numbers for text messages (§1006.6(d)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: A debt collector may send texts to a telephone number if (i) the consumer used that number to text the collector about the debt and hasn't opted out and within 60 days consumer sent the text or the collector confirmed number not reassigned, or (ii) collector received direct prior consent to text and consumer hasn't withdrawn it and within 60 days consent was obtained/renewed or collector confirmed number not reassigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires using a complete and accurate database to confirm reassignment where applicable; consent must be current within the specified 60-day windows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opt-out notice for electronic communications (§1006.6(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any electronic communication (email, text, other electronic-medium) used by a debt collector to communicate about a debt must include a clear and conspicuous statement describing a reasonable and simple method by which the consumer can opt out of further electronic communications to that address/number. Collectors may not condition opt-out on payment or require information beyond opt-out preferences and the address/number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opt-out mechanism must be simple and free; debt collectors cannot require fees or extraneous information to process opt-out requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquisition of location information — form and content (§1006.10(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: When communicating with a person other than the consumer to acquire location information, the debt collector must: identify themself individually by name, state they are confirming/correcting location info, and only if expressly requested identify employer; must not state that the consumer owes any debt; must not communicate by postcard; must not use language/symbol on envelopes indicating debt collection; and after knowing consumer represented by counsel, must not communicate with others except attorney unless attorney fails to respond timely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule protects confidentiality of debt and limits what can be communicated when seeking location info; strict envelope/mail content limitations are specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquisition of location information — frequency limitation (§1006.10(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A debt collector must not communicate more than once with a person (other than the consumer) for location information unless requested by that person or the collector reasonably believes the earlier response was erroneous or incomplete and that the person now has correct/complete info.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must also comply with §1006.14(b)(1) regarding harassing, oppressive, or abusive conduct; one-contact presumption unless justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: General prohibition on harassing, oppressive, or abusive conduct (§1006.14(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Debt collectors must not engage in conduct the natural consequence of which is to harass, oppress, or abuse any person in connection with debt collection, including conduct described in paragraphs (b) through (h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section then enumerates examples (telephone call frequency, threats, obscene language, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeated/continuous telephone calls — frequency limits and presumptions (§1006.14(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Debt collectors must not place telephone calls or engage in telephone conversations repeatedly or continuously with intent to annoy, abuse, or harass. Presumption of compliance: not more than seven calls within seven consecutive days to a particular person in connection with a particular debt, nor within seven days after a telephone conversation about that debt. Exceeding those frequencies is presumed a violation, subject to exclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusions include calls made with prior consent (within seven days), calls not connected to dialed number, or calls to parties listed in §1006.6(d)(1)(ii)-(vi). Defines 'particular debt' (separate debts; student loans serviced under single account treated differently).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on violence or criminal threats (§1006.14(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Debt collectors must not use or threaten to use violence or other criminal means to harm the physical person, reputation, or property of any person in connection with debt collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Zero-tolerance prohibition; absolute bar on threats of illegal action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on obscene or profane language (§1006.14(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Debt collectors must not use obscene or profane language, or language the natural consequence of which is to abuse the hearer or reader, in connection with debt collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers written and oral communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on publishing debtor lists (§1006.14(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Debt collectors must not publish a list of consumers who allegedly refuse to pay debts, except to a consumer reporting agency or to persons meeting certain FCRA requirements (sections 603(f) or 604(a)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects against public shaming via publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on coercive advertisements (§1006.14(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Debt collectors must not advertise for sale any debt to coerce payment of the debt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advertising debts for sale cannot be used as a coercive collection method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaningful disclosure of identity when calling (§1006.14(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Debt collectors must not place telephone calls without meaningfully disclosing the caller's identity, except as provided in §1006.10.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents anonymous harassing calls; meaningful disclosure differs from full disclosure in other sections but requires identification consistent with applicable rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited communication media and exceptions (§1006.14(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Debt collectors must not communicate through a medium requested by a person not to be used, but exceptions allow (i) an electronic confirmation of an opt-out (containing only confirmation), (ii) a one-time response if the person initiates contact via that medium, or (iii) communications required by applicable law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects consumer-selected communication preferences with limited, narrow exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: General prohibition on false, deceptive, or misleading representations (§1006.18(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Debt collectors must not use any false, deceptive, or misleading representation or means to collect a debt, including specified examples in paragraphs (b) through (d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section (b)-(d) lists many specific prohibitions and illustrative examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific false or deceptive representations prohibited (§1006.18(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A debt collector must not falsely represent or imply, among other things, that they are affiliated with the U.S. or a State; that they operate as a consumer reporting agency; that any individual is an attorney or communication is from an attorney; that the consumer committed a crime; that sale/transfer of a debt causes loss of defenses; that accounts turned over to innocent purchasers; that documents are legal process; or that documents do not require action. Also must not falsely represent character/amount/legal status of debt or services/compensation, nor imply nonpayment will result in arrest or seizure unless lawful and intended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits a wide range of misrepresentations about status, authority, legal consequences, and document authenticity; intent and factual basis are relevant to some items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on false collection means and threatening unlawful action (§1006.18(c)–(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Collectors must not threaten to take any action that cannot legally be taken or is not intended; must not communicate false credit information; must not use or distribute communications that simulate court or official documents or create false impressions about source/approval; must not use any business name other than the true name of the debt collector's organization (subject to assumed-name rule); and must not use false or deceptive means to collect debts or obtain consumer information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes explicit ban on simulating legal process and on using misleading business names; assumed-name exception discussed in §1006.18(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required disclosures in initial and subsequent communications (§1006.18(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: In initial communication, debt collectors must disclose they are attempting to collect a debt and that information obtained will be used for that purpose; if initial contact is oral, the disclosure must be repeated in the first written communication. In subsequent communications, each communication must disclose it is from a debt collector. Disclosures need not be in formal pleadings. Disclosures must be in the same language used for the rest of the communication; translations must be complete and accurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translations must be complete and accurate; the Bureau's website language is considered a complete/accurate translation for validation notices (§1006.34 comment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumed names permitted under conditions (§1006.18(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Debt collector employees may use an assumed name when communicating, provided the assumed name is used consistently and the debt collector can readily identify any employee using that assumed name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows limited use of aliases for employee privacy but requires internal traceability and consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfair or unconscionable means prohibition (§1006.22(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Debt collectors must not use unfair or unconscionable means to collect debts, including the specific conduct described in paragraphs (b) through (f) (collection of unauthorized amounts, postdated instruments rules, concealment charges, nonjudicial action regarding property, restrictions on use of certain media).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a catch-all prohibition augmented by specified actionable examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on collecting unauthorized amounts (§1006.22(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Collectors must not collect any amount unless expressly authorized by the agreement creating the debt or permitted by law; 'any amount' includes interest, fees, charges, expenses incidental to principal obligation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict limitation on adding or collecting fees not contractually or legally authorized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for postdated payment instruments (§1006.22(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Collectors must not accept checks or payment instruments postdated by more than five days unless giving written notice 3–10 days prior to deposit; must not solicit postdated instruments to threaten criminal prosecution; must not deposit or threaten to deposit before the date on the instrument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies timing for notice (not more than 10 nor less than 3 days before deposit) and forbids misuse of postdated instruments for coercion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on charges from concealment of purpose (§1006.22(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Collectors must not cause charges to be made to any person by concealing the true purpose of the communication (e.g., collect telephone calls, telegram fees).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bars shifting communication costs to consumers through deception about the communication's purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on nonjudicial action regarding property (§1006.22(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Collectors must not take or threaten nonjudicial action to dispossess or disable property if (1) there is no present right to possession through enforceable security interest, (2) no present intention to take possession, or (3) the property is exempt by law from dispossession/disablement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents false or empty threats to seize property; requires actual present enforceable rights and intention to act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on use of certain media (§1006.22(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Collectors must not: communicate by postcard; use any language or symbol on envelopes other than address (with limited business-name exception that doesn't indicate debt collection); email addresses provided by employer unless permitted under §1006.6(d)(4)(i)/(iii); or communicate via social media in a manner viewable by general public or person's social media contacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits media that could disclose debt to third parties or public; social-media communications must not be publicly viewable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safe harbor for certain emails and texts (§1006.22(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: A collector who communicates by email or text in accordance with procedures in §1006.6(d)(3) does not violate the unfair/unconscionable prohibition by revealing the collector's name or other info indicating the communication relates to collection of a debt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides safe harbor when the collector followed the required procedures for email/text use (address provenance, consent, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection of time-barred debts prohibited (§1006.26(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Collectors must not bring or threaten to bring a legal action against a consumer to collect a time-barred debt (statute of limitations expired). Exception: proofs of claim in bankruptcy proceedings are not covered by this paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separately defines 'statute of limitations' and 'time-barred debt' in (a). Collectors may not use legal-action threats to coerce payment on stale debts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required actions before furnishing information to a consumer reporting agency (§1006.30(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Collectors must not furnish information about a debt to a consumer reporting agency before they either (i) speak to the consumer in person or by telephone about the debt, or (ii) place a letter or electronic message and wait a reasonable period to receive undeliverability notice (monitoring notifications). If an undeliverability notification is received during the period, the collector must not furnish information until the requirement is otherwise satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects against furnishing debt info when initial contact attempts fail; monitoring for undeliverability is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special rule for furnishing to certain specialty consumer reporting agencies (§1006.30(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraph (a)(1) does not apply to furnishing information about a debt to a nationwide specialty consumer reporting agency; special rules may apply (text truncated on page).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collectors must consult the full text for detailed carve-outs and procedures applicable to specialty CRAs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation notice content and permitted modifications (§1006.34 and comments)
rubrics_metrics.description: The validation (debt validation) notice must contain consumer-response information and required disclosures; permitted modifications include relocating consumer-response info for mailing, adding barcodes/QR codes (so long as §1006.38(b) not violated), adding generation date, embedding hyperlinks for electronic delivery, including telephone contact info, and including disclosures required by applicable law on reverse or below notice content. Collectors may include merchant/affinity/facility brands and supplemental Spanish-language info on how to request a Spanish-language validation notice. Translations must be complete and accurate; the Bureau's website translation is a safe harbor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments provide many examples and permissible optional disclosures (telephone contact info, time-barred disclosures if required by law, statements referring to disclosures on reverse or below, Spanish supplemental statements, examples of merchant/affinity/facility brand use). Translation safe harbor: using Bureau-provided language is considered complete and accurate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disputes and requests for original-creditor information (§1006.38) — written submissions and E-SIGN interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements related to disputes or requests for the original creditor's name/address timely submitted in writing: written includes mailed disputes, returned consumer-response form, electronic medium the collector accepts (email/portal), or in-person/courier delivery. Bureau interprets E-SIGN to allow electronic requests if the collector accepts that medium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies acceptable media for 'in writing' under §1006.38 and interprets E-SIGN Act applicability; collectors must accept disputes by electronic means only if they accept that medium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicative dispute standard and new & material information (§1006.38(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A dispute is duplicative if substantially the same as a prior written dispute submitted within the validation period for which the collector already satisfied §1006.38(d)(2)(i). A later dispute is not duplicative if the consumer provides new and material information (new = not previously provided; material = reasonably likely to change the verification). Example: submitting a cancelled check after an earlier unsupported dispute is new and material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collectors must evaluate whether new information would reasonably change verification; duplicative-dispute procedures differ from ordinary dispute handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response to duplicative disputes (§1006.38(d)(2)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the collector reasonably determines a dispute is duplicative, the collector must cease collection of the debt or disputed portion until it either (A) notifies the consumer the dispute is duplicative (providing a brief statement of reasons and referring to prior response), or (B) provides a copy of verification of the debt or judgment. The duplicative notice must state the dispute is substantially the same and provide date of the earlier response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While collection ceases, the collector must either provide verification or explain briefly why dispute is duplicative and refer to earlier response (including date).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sending required disclosures in manner reasonably expected to provide actual notice (§1006.42(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: When sending required disclosures in writing or electronically, collectors must do so in a manner reasonably expected to provide actual notice. Relevant factors include: identifying purpose in subject line (creditor name and one additional identifier other than amount), permitting/monitoring undeliverability notifications and treating undeliverability as precluding actual notice, and identifying sender by a business name consumer would recognize (e.g., as used in prior limited-content messages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to monitor undeliverability or receiving undeliverability notice means not reasonably expected to provide actual notice; subject-line identification examples include truncated account number, original creditor name, store brand, date of sale, physical address of service, billing/mailing address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of undeliverability and safe harbor for mail (§1006.42(a)(2)–(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a collector receives notice the disclosure was not delivered, they have not sent the disclosure in a manner reasonably expected to provide actual notice. A safe harbor exists for disclosures sent by mail: mailing a printed copy to the consumer's last known address satisfies §1006.42(a)(1), unless at mailing time the collector knows or should know the consumer does not reside at or receive mail at that location.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collectors must evaluate known address information at time of mailing; monitoring for delivery failure notifications is important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of consumer opt-outs on sending required disclosures (§1006.42(a)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a consumer has opted out of communications to a particular email or telephone number, the collector cannot use that address/number to send required disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consumer opt-out preferences override the collector's ability to use that medium for mandatory disclosures; collectors must track opt-outs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record retention — three-year retention period and scope (§1006.100)
rubrics_metrics.description: Collectors must retain records that are evidence of compliance or noncompliance with the FDCPA and Regulation F from the date they begin collection activity on a debt until three years after the last collection activity on the debt. Telephone call recordings must be retained for three years after the dates of the calls if recordings are made. Collectors may retain records longer but not less than three years for evidentiary records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of records to retain include telephone call logs evidencing compliance with §1006.14(b)(1) and copies of documents provided to consumers to show compliance with §§1006.34 and 1006.38 and delivery requirements under §1006.42. Record types that could evidence compliance or noncompliance depending on conduct must be retained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special rule for telephone call recordings (§1006.100(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Collectors are not required to record telephone calls. However, if they do record calls, each recording is evidence of compliance/noncompliance and must be retained for three years after the call date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recording is optional but creates a mandatory retention obligation for recordings made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation to State laws — disclosure requirements (§1006.104)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulation F and the FDCPA do not annul, alter, or exempt persons from complying with State disclosure requirements that provide additional consumer protections not inconsistent with the FDCPA or Regulation F. A State-required disclosure is not inconsistent if it affords consumers greater protection than the FDCPA/Regulation F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collectors must comply with applicable State law disclosure requirements that are more protective; Regulation F does not preempt State protections that are consistent or more protective.
